problem: Prior VLN methods represent explored environments with recurrent states, topological graphs, or grid maps, which struggle to capture multi-level spatial information (waypoints, objects, rooms, floors), and their semantic feature extraction is not robust to viewpoint changes.
motivation: Accurate multi-granularity spatial representation and view-robust object features are needed to ground instructions that refer to objects, rooms, and floors. Limited observation coverage from fixed viewpoints degrades feature quality, so novel-view synthesis could help.
key_idea: Build a multi-layer map (waypoints, objects, rooms, floors) encoded by a heterogeneous graph transformer and aligned with instructions, and use 3D Gaussian splatting to render novel views for viewpoint-robust object feature extraction.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that explicit multi-level spatial structure and 3DGS-based novel-view observation improve planning and feature robustness respectively.
method: Multi-layer map: models the scene at several granularities, with waypoint, object, room and floor nodes.
Heterogeneous graph transformer: extracts spatial features from the multi-layer map, handling different node and edge types.
Instruction alignment: aligns the spatial features with the language instruction to guide planning.
3D Gaussian splatting: captures 3D geometry and texture, enabling novel-view object observation.
Viewpoint-robust feature extraction: extracts features from rendered novel views to improve observation coverage and robustness.
